record.question: A Superintendent of Police writes an article on police modernization for a professional journal. The article contains no criticism of Government policy but includes information obtained during official meetings that has not been released to the public. The article is published after obtaining permission from the editor but not from the Government. Which is the most legally correct conclusion?
options: No violation because the article is academic in nature
No violation because there is no criticism of Government
The officer may violate CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 relating to communication of official information
The officer is liable only if the information is subsequently published by newspapers
